 Gabe Hauari USA TODAY Oct. 27, 2026, 8:51 a.m. ET Hear this story Toyota is recalling more than 228,000 vehicles in the United States due to an issue with the second-row seat backs, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.
 According to the recall notice posted by the NHTSA , the seat backs may fail to remain secured in the event of a crash, which may fail to properly protect an occupant, increasing the risk of injury.
 The total number of vehicles affected by this recall is 228,367.
 Here's what to know about the model included in the recall and what car owners can do to get the issue fixed.
 More car recalls: Volkswagen recalls over 9,000 Audi vehicles. See affected models What model is included in the recall?
 The recall includes certain 2022-2026 Toyota Sienna Hybrid 7-passengers vehicles.

See affected models Volvo recalls more than 9,000 vehicles. See affected models Ford recalls more than 102K vehicles. See the affected models What car owners should do
 According to the recall notice, dealers will update the supplemental restraint system (SRS) electronic control unit (ECU) software.
 For vehicles equipped with the "Mobility as a Service" (MaaS) package, dealers will replace the two second-row seat backs. Repairs will be performed free of charge.
 Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed Dec. 7, 2026. Owners may contact Toyota's customer service at 1-800-331-4331. Toyota's numbers for this recall are 26TB24 and 26TA24.
